props.gloss_en: were it not for the maamadot, heaven and earth would not endure
Rav Asi's verse for it: 'and he said, Lord God, by what shall I know that I shall inherit it?' (Gen 15:8)
to Abraham's 'if Israel sin before You, will You do to them as to the generation of the flood and of the dispersion?' God answered: no

to 'tell me, by what shall I inherit it?' God answered with 'take for Me a three-year-old heifer and a three-year-old goat...' (Gen 15:9). (That this alludes to the offerings is Steinsaltz's explanation, not the text's.)

to 'granted while the Temple stands; when it does not, what will become of them?' God answered: I have already instituted for them the order of offerings; when they read it before Me I account it as though they had offered them, and I forgive all their sins
the men of the mishmar would pray over their brothers' offering that it be accepted with favour
the men of the maamad assemble in the synagogue and keep four fasts: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday
on Tuesday -- for those travelling the deserts
on Wednesday -- against croup, that it not fall upon the children
on Thursday -- for pregnant and nursing women: the pregnant, that they not miscarry; the nursing, that they nurse their children
on Friday they would not fast, for the honour of Shabbat
all the more so they would not fast on Shabbat itself
the presupposition of the stam's question: the maamad did not fast on Sunday
R' Yochanan: because of the notzrim
R' Shmuel bar Nachmani: because it is the third day from creation
Reish Lakish: because of the added soul
Reish Lakish's dictum: an added soul is given to a person on Shabbat eve, and at Shabbat's end it is taken from him
his verse: 'He ceased and rested [vayinafash]' (Ex 31:17) -- once he has ceased, woe (vai), the soul (nefesh) is lost
